headline_marked: Hasan Mahmud takes [[first-ever Bangladeshi pacer Test hat-trick]] against Afghanistan
headline: Hasan Mahmud takes first-ever Bangladeshi pacer Test hat-trick against Afghanistan
summary: The right-arm pacer's stunning burst reduced Afghanistan to 220-8, helping Bangladesh secure a 106-run lead in the one-off Test in Abu Dhabi.
details: Hasan Mahmud has become the first Bangladeshi fast bowler to claim a Test hat-trick, ripping through Afghanistan's lower order on the third morning of the one-off Test in Abu Dhabi.
In a dramatic burst, Hasan struck with three successive deliveries in his 18th over, reducing Afghanistan to 220-8 in response to Bangladesh's first-innings total of 346.
He bowled Ismat Alam for one, followed by a clean-bowled Qais Ahmad and an LBW dismissal of Zia-ur-Rehman Akbar, who was confirmed via review.
Hasan is only the third Bangladeshi player overall to achieve a Test hat-trick, joining Alok Kapali (2003) and Sohag Gazi (2013).
The collapse was a sudden reversal for Afghanistan, who had previously built a stubborn 80-run partnership between captain Rahmat Shah and Ikram Alikhil.
Ebadot Hossain broke the partnership by bowling Ikram for 32, which paved the way for Hasan's historic achievement.
Afghanistan was eventually bowled out for 240, giving the Tigers a 106-run lead as they prepare for their third innings.
Bangladesh's first innings was led by Tanzid Hasan (83), Shadman Islam (67), and Litton Das (53) to post a total of 346.
caption:
History made! Hasan Mahmud becomes the first Bangladeshi fast bowler to take a Test hat-trick.

Hasan Mahmud has become the first Bangladeshi fast bowler to claim a Test hat-trick, ripping through Afghanistan's lower order on the third morning of the one-off Test in Abu Dhabi.

In a dramatic burst, Hasan struck with three successive deliveries in his 18th over, reducing Afghanistan to 220-8 in response to Bangladesh's first-innings total of 346.

He bowled Ismat Alam for one, followed by a clean-bowled Qais Ahmad and an LBW dismissal of Zia-ur-Rehman Akbar, who was confirmed via review.

Hasan is only the third Bangladeshi player overall to achieve a Test hat-trick, joining Alok Kapali (2003) and Sohag Gazi (2013).

The collapse was a sudden reversal for Afghanistan, who had previously built a stubborn 80-run partnership between captain Rahmat Shah and Ikram Alikhil.

Ebadot Hossain broke the partnership by bowling Ikram for 32, which paved the way for Hasan's historic achievement.

Afghanistan was eventually bowled out for 240, giving the Tigers a 106-run lead as they prepare for their third innings.

Bangladesh's first innings was led by Tanzid Hasan (83), Shadman Islam (67), and Litton Das (53) to post a total of 346.

headline_marked: 12 killed, 300 injured as [[Houthi attack hits Riyadh airport]]
headline: 12 killed, 300 injured as Houthi attack hits Riyadh airport
summary: Two Bangladeshis are among the dead. At least seven flights from Dhaka to Riyadh have been cancelled following the facility's closure.
details: At least 12 people were killed and 300 others injured in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, carried out by Houthi rebels.
Among the casualties, two Bangladeshi nationals were killed, according to reports. Bangladesh has strongly condemned the attack and is working to identify the victims.
The attack led to the suspension of operations at the airport, causing significant travel disruptions for passengers traveling between Dhaka and Riyadh.
As of 1:00 pm today, at least seven flights from Dhaka to Riyadh have been cancelled, affecting both Biman Bangladesh Airlines and Saudi carriers.
Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended its Dhaka-Riyadh-Dhaka flights BG339 and BG340 until further notice, advising passengers not to proceed to the airport.
Additionally, US-Bangla Airlines flight BS381, bound for Riyadh, was diverted to Muscat, Oman, before returning to Dhaka early this morning.
The United Nations Secretary-General and the Arab League have also expressed deep shock and condemnation of the attack.
caption:
12 dead and 300 injured after a Houthi attack on Riyadh airport—including two Bangladeshis.

At least 12 people were killed and 300 others injured in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, carried out by Houthi rebels.

Among the casualties, two Bangladeshi nationals were killed, according to reports. Bangladesh has strongly condemned the attack and is working to identify the victims.

The attack led to the suspension of operations at the airport, causing significant travel disruptions for passengers traveling between Dhaka and Riyadh.

As of 1:00 pm today, at least seven flights from Dhaka to Riyadh have been cancelled, affecting both Biman Bangladesh Airlines and Saudi carriers.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended its Dhaka-Riyadh-Dhaka flights BG339 and BG340 until further notice, advising passengers not to proceed to the airport.

Additionally, US-Bangla Airlines flight BS381, bound for Riyadh, was diverted to Muscat, Oman, before returning to Dhaka early this morning.

The United Nations Secretary-General and the Arab League have also expressed deep shock and condemnation of the attack.
